title: Which fraction is bigger? Start with the whole
description: Compare equal-size strips before relying on the written numbers, and learn two useful shortcuts.

cover.alt: Different-sized flatbread wedges on two matching plates
cover.credit: AI-generated photorealistic image created for BrainiLab.

hub.name: Fractions, one piece at a time

practice: Try a few problems at your own pace, then return to any explanation you want to revisit.

sections.title: Use the same starting size
sections.html:
Imagine two identical chocolate bars. One person has three fifths of a bar and another has two fifths. Because every fifth has the same size, three fifths is more.

That gives a simple rule: when the denominators are equal, compare the numerators. You are counting the same kind of piece. Four sevenths is more than two sevenths for the same reason.

sections.title: Try it yourself
sections.html:
Change the selected parts on two strips of equal length. First keep both denominators the same. Then try one half against one quarter.

One half is larger even though two is smaller than four. With one selected part in each fraction, a larger denominator means the whole was split into more, smaller pieces. The bottom number is not a score where higher always wins.

sections.title: Find a shared kind of piece
sections.html:
What about 2/3 and 3/4? The numerators and denominators both differ, so neither simple shortcut is enough. Rename both fractions in twelfths: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12.

Now the pieces match. Nine twelfths is more than eight twelfths, so three quarters is larger than two thirds. The equivalent fractions changed the labels, not the original amounts.

sections.title: Use a halfway check
sections.html:
A half can help you estimate. Three eighths is below a half because four eighths would be a half. Five eighths is above a half. This quick check can rule out an answer before you do a longer calculation.

Keep the whole in mind: half a large cake may be more food than three quarters of a small cake. Our strip comparisons use equal wholes, which is why the fraction values alone are enough.

questions.prompt: Which is larger for the same whole?
questions.explanation: Both use sevenths; four such pieces exceed two.

questions.prompt: Which is larger: 1/2 or 1/4 of the same whole?
questions.explanation: Halves are larger pieces than quarters.
They are 8/12 and 9/12 respectively, so three quarters is larger.
